subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw support a stable external agent-runtime contract for non-Node and embedded hosts, or keep the Node-hosted Gateway as the supported runtime boundary?
rationale: This is a large product and compatibility commitment: choosing the contract determines which session, tool, auth, streaming, persistence, and security semantics become supported outside the current process.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow portability RFC
options.body: Define a minimal external runtime protocol and conformance scope before approving any language, WASM, or embedded implementation.

options.title: Keep Node as the supported runtime
options.body: Treat external projects such as MimiClaw as independent implementations and retain only current Gateway/plugin extension seams.

options.title: Extend plugin IPC first
options.body: Advance the language-agnostic plugin boundary in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98004, then reassess whether it exposes a genuine embedded-runtime gap.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow portability RFC
recommendation.body: Define a minimal external runtime protocol and conformance scope before approving any language, WASM, or embedded implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged agent-runtime ownership refactor and the existing issue response make this the clearest available routing candidate for the runtime-boundary decision.
